history.period: 18th century (approx 250 years old per local accounts; exact date unverified)
history.summary: Hindu temple dedicated to Goddess Durga on the banks of a former drought pond (now converted into a public park) on Devi Mandir Road, Tehsil Camp, Panipat. Local accounts say Maratha leader Sadashivrao Bhau found a Devi idol on the tank's bank before the Third Battle of Panipat (1761) and built the temple around it; one source (inheritage.foundation) instead attributes construction to Maratha sardar Bhaskar Rao Ramchandra Pandit and calls the goddess Bhadrakali — CONFLICT (verify). Legend says the idol, when moved overnight during construction, returned to its original spot by morning. Exact founding date is unverified; the 18th-century attribution is from secondary web sources only.

name: Shri Devi Mandir
town_description: Panipat is a historic city in Haryana on the Grand Trunk Road (NH-44), about 90 km north of Delhi, famous for three pivotal battles (1526, 1556, 1761) that shaped Indian history. Today it is one of India's largest centres for handloom weaving, blankets and carpets, and an industrial hub in the National Capital Region. Its dense mix of Mughal-era and Maratha-era heritage sites draws both pilgrims and history tourists.
